Our ask
Healthcare, Biotechnology & Social Innovation

Affordable Diagnostics for Every Community

“Early Detection. Affordable Healthcare. Healthier Communities.”

Jeevan Tech is a proposed affordable diagnostic service that partners with existing laboratories, primary healthcare centres and community clinics to make basic health screening more accessible in rural and semi-urban India.

The problem: why now?

“A healthcare problem should never go undetected simply because a diagnostic service is too far away or difficult to access.” Many rural and semi-urban communities face practical barriers to convenient, timely diagnostic services.

Accessibility

Patients may need to travel to larger towns for certain tests.

Affordability

Transport costs and repeated visits add to the burden of healthcare.

Fragmentation

Patients may need to coordinate appointments, sample collection and test reports across different providers.

Business gap

Smaller clinics may lack the infrastructure to offer a broad range of tests themselves.

Why now? India has been expanding primary healthcare access and free diagnostic services, creating opportunities to complement existing facilities with better coordination and reach.

Our opportunity: build a convenient, affordable diagnostic access network without investing in a full laboratory at every location.

The solution: a hub-and-spoke diagnostic network

Jeevan Tech connects local collection points with qualified partner laboratories, using digital appointment management, sample collection coordination and secure delivery of results.

Unique value proposition: more convenient access, coordinated service delivery and lower infrastructure investment through partnerships.

MVP: launch with routine blood tests and preventive screening packages using existing accredited laboratory partners. Jeevan Tech coordinates services rather than manufacturing diagnostic kits or independently diagnosing patients.

Go-to-market and scalability

Phase 1Months 1–6

Pilot launch in Andhra Pradesh

  • Partner with 2–3 existing diagnostic laboratories
  • Onboard 5 local clinics or collection points
  • Test booking, sample transport, reporting and customer feedback
  • Track turnaround time, service quality and affordability
Phase 2Months 7–12

Regional expansion

  • Expand to nearby semi-urban and rural catchments
  • Introduce employer and clinic subscription agreements
  • Improve logistics using demand and route data
Phase 3Months 13–18

Scalable expansion

  • Enter selected Hyderabad and Telangana catchments
  • Build institutional partnerships
  • Standardize operating procedures before entering additional regions

Potential strategic partners: accredited diagnostic laboratories, hospitals, primary healthcare providers, health-tech platforms and university incubators. Corporate innovation programmes from companies such as IBM, Wipro or Accenture may be explored where relevant, but no partnership is assumed to be secured.

Implementation roadmap and risk mitigation

18-month timeline

Risk 1: sample quality or transport delays

Use validated packaging, documented handling procedures, temperature controls where required, scheduled pickups and backup logistics providers.

Risk 2: low adoption or weak margins

Start with a limited pilot, conduct customer research, partner with trusted clinics and adjust the service mix based on demand.

Compliance checklist: before launch, assess applicable Clinical Establishments legislation and state rules, biomedical waste management requirements, laboratory quality standards, patient consent and data privacy requirements, and relevant health-facility registrations. Confirm applicability with qualified regulatory advisers rather than assuming a single national approval covers all operations.
